sections.title: The Encouragement to Rebuild the Temple
observations: In this section, God addresses the people through Haggai, reminding them of the importance of the temple and the glory it once had. The people are discouraged by the current state of the temple, which pales in comparison to Solomon's temple. God reassures them that He is with them and encourages them to be strong and continue their work.

The call to be strong is significant as it reflects God's desire for His people to persevere in their tasks despite challenges. The promise of God's presence is a central theme, emphasizing that their efforts are not in vain.

sections.title: The Promise of Future Glory
observations: God promises that the glory of the latter temple will surpass that of the former. This is a profound statement that not only speaks to the physical rebuilding of the temple but also points to the coming of Christ, who would fulfill the ultimate purpose of the temple as the dwelling place of God among His people.

The shaking of the heavens and the earth signifies God's sovereignty over all creation and His ability to bring about change. The treasures of the nations being brought to the temple foreshadows the inclusion of the Gentiles in God's redemptive plan.

sections.title: The Significance of Holiness
observations: Haggai emphasizes the importance of holiness and how it affects the people. The analogy of the unclean and the clean illustrates that sin can contaminate even the most sacred of activities. This serves as a reminder that the people's relationship with God is paramount and that their actions have consequences.
The call to consider their ways is a recurring theme in Haggai, urging the people to reflect on their priorities and their relationship with God.

importantVerses.commentary: 'Yet now be strong, O Zerubbabel, declares the LORD. Be strong, O Joshua, son of Jehozadak, the high priest; be strong, all you people of the land, declares the LORD. Work, for I am with you, declares the LORD of hosts.' This verse emphasizes God's presence and encouragement to His people as they undertake the rebuilding of the temple.

'The latter glory of this house shall be greater than the former, says the LORD of hosts. And in this place I will give peace, declares the LORD of hosts.' This verse points to the future glory of the temple and the peace that God promises to His people.

questions: What does it mean for God to be with His people during difficult times?
How does the promise of future glory in the temple relate to the New Testament understanding of Christ?
In what ways can we apply the call to consider our ways in our own lives today?
